topico: glicogenio (treino de estilo AnKing — SANDBOX, nao vai pro deck vivo)
nota: v2: crédito Physeo herdado (imagem é Physeo); GSD usam img_gsd + formato/mnemonico AnKing; verso telegrafico.

cards.Text: Glycogen is a branched storage polymer of {{c1::glucose}}
cards.Extra: Highly branched for rapid mobilization. Image licensed by Physeo and used with permission. Purchase full access here.

cards.Text: The linear glucose linkages in glycogen are {{c1::α-1,4}} glycosidic bonds
cards.Extra: Image licensed by Physeo and used with permission. Purchase full access here.

cards.Text: The branch-point linkages in glycogen are {{c1::α-1,6}} glycosidic bonds
cards.Extra: Every 8-10 residues. Image licensed by Physeo and used with permission. Purchase full access here.

cards.Text: Glycogen is stored mainly in {{c1::liver}} and {{c2::skeletal muscle}}
cards.Extra: Image licensed by Physeo and used with permission. Purchase full access here.

cards.Text: Glycogen synthesis is nucleated by the primer protein {{c1::glycogenin}}
cards.Extra: Autoglucosylates the first residues. Image licensed by Physeo and used with permission. Purchase full access here.

cards.Text: The activated glucose donor for glycogen synthesis is {{c1::UDP-glucose}}
cards.Extra: Image licensed by Physeo and used with permission. Purchase full access here.

cards.Text: Glucose-6-phosphate is converted to glucose-1-phosphate by {{c1::phosphoglucomutase}}
cards.Extra: Reversible. Image licensed by Physeo and used with permission. Purchase full access here.

cards.Text: UDP-glucose is formed from glucose-1-phosphate by {{c1::UDP-glucose pyrophosphorylase}}
cards.Extra: Driven by PPi hydrolysis. Image licensed by Physeo and used with permission. Purchase full access here.

cards.Text: The rate-limiting enzyme of glycogenesis is {{c1::glycogen synthase}}
cards.Extra: Adds glucose via α-1,4 bonds. Image licensed by Physeo and used with permission. Purchase full access here.

cards.Text: Branches in glycogen are created by {{c1::branching enzyme}}
cards.Extra: Transfers a ~7-residue block to an α-1,6 position. Image licensed by Physeo and used with permission. Purchase full access here.

cards.Text: The rate-limiting enzyme of glycogenolysis is {{c1::glycogen phosphorylase}}
cards.Extra: Image licensed by Physeo and used with permission. Purchase full access here.

cards.Text: Glycogen phosphorylase cleaves α-1,4 bonds by {{c1::phosphorolysis}}, releasing glucose-1-phosphate
cards.Extra: Uses Pi, not water. Image licensed by Physeo and used with permission. Purchase full access here.

cards.Text: Glycogen phosphorylase requires the cofactor {{c1::pyridoxal phosphate}} (vitamin B6)
cards.Extra: Image licensed by Physeo and used with permission. Purchase full access here.

cards.Text: Glycogen phosphorylase stops {{c1::4}} residues from a branch point, leaving a limit dextrin
cards.Extra: Image licensed by Physeo and used with permission. Purchase full access here.

cards.Text: The {{c1::debranching enzyme}} removes the α-1,6 branch, releasing free glucose
cards.Extra: 4-α-glucanotransferase + α-1,6-glucosidase activities. Image licensed by Physeo and used with permission. Purchase full access here.

cards.Text: About {{c1::8}}% of glycogen is released as free glucose (from branch points); the rest is glucose-1-phosphate
cards.Extra: Image licensed by Physeo and used with permission. Purchase full access here.

cards.Text: Glycogen synthase is active when {{c1::dephosphorylated}}
cards.Extra: Insulin state. Image licensed by Physeo and used with permission. Purchase full access here.

cards.Text: Glycogen phosphorylase is active when {{c1::phosphorylated}}
cards.Extra: Glucagon/epinephrine state. Image licensed by Physeo and used with permission. Purchase full access here.

cards.Text: Glucagon and epinephrine raise {{c1::cAMP}} via adenylyl cyclase
cards.Extra: Image licensed by Physeo and used with permission. Purchase full access here.

cards.Text: cAMP activates {{c1::protein kinase A}} (PKA)
cards.Extra: Image licensed by Physeo and used with permission. Purchase full access here.

cards.Text: PKA phosphorylates and activates {{c1::phosphorylase kinase}}
cards.Extra: Image licensed by Physeo and used with permission. Purchase full access here.

cards.Text: Phosphorylase kinase phosphorylates and activates {{c1::glycogen phosphorylase}}
cards.Extra: Image licensed by Physeo and used with permission. Purchase full access here.

cards.Text: PKA also phosphorylates and {{c1::inactivates}} glycogen synthase
cards.Extra: One signal: breakdown on, synthesis off. Image licensed by Physeo and used with permission. Purchase full access here.

cards.Text: Insulin activates {{c1::protein phosphatase 1}} (PP1)
cards.Extra: Dephosphorylates the cascade: synthesis on, breakdown off. Image licensed by Physeo and used with permission. Purchase full access here.

cards.Text: In liver, glucose binds phosphorylase a and exposes it to {{c1::PP1}}
cards.Extra: Links high glucose to storage. Image licensed by Physeo and used with permission. Purchase full access here.

cards.Text: Glycogen synthase is allosterically activated by {{c1::glucose-6-phosphate}}
cards.Extra: Image licensed by Physeo and used with permission. Purchase full access here.

cards.Text: In muscle, glycogen phosphorylase b is allosterically activated by {{c1::AMP}}
cards.Extra: Signals low energy. Image licensed by Physeo and used with permission. Purchase full access here.

cards.Text: In muscle, glycogen phosphorylase is activated by {{c1::Ca2+}}/calmodulin during contraction
cards.Extra: Calmodulin is a subunit of phosphorylase kinase. Image licensed by Physeo and used with permission. Purchase full access here.

cards.Text: Muscle epinephrine acts on glycogen via {{c1::β-adrenergic}} receptors
cards.Extra: Gs, cAMP. Image licensed by Physeo and used with permission. Purchase full access here.

cards.Text: Liver glycogen serves to maintain {{c1::blood glucose}}
cards.Extra: Image licensed by Physeo and used with permission. Purchase full access here.

cards.Text: Muscle glycogen fuels {{c1::the muscle itself}} (cannot export glucose)
cards.Extra: Image licensed by Physeo and used with permission. Purchase full access here.

cards.Text: Muscle cannot release free glucose because it lacks {{c1::glucose-6-phosphatase}}
cards.Extra: Image licensed by Physeo and used with permission. Purchase full access here.

cards.Text: Free glucose is released from glucose-6-phosphate by {{c1::glucose-6-phosphatase}} in the ER
cards.Extra: Liver, kidney, gut only. Image licensed by Physeo and used with permission. Purchase full access here.

cards.Text: {{c2::Von Gierke}} disease is also known as glycogen storage disease type {{c1::I}}
cards.Extra: Von Gierke = One Gierke (type 1). Deficiency of glucose-6-phosphatase. Image licensed by Physeo and used with permission. Purchase full access here.

cards.Text: Von Gierke disease presents with severe fasting {{c1::hypoglycemia}} and hepatomegaly
cards.Extra: Also lactic acidosis, hyperuricemia, hyperlipidemia. Image licensed by Physeo and used with permission. Purchase full access here.

cards.Text: {{c2::Pompe}} disease (glycogen storage disease type {{c1::II}}) is deficiency of lysosomal {{c3::acid α-glucosidase}} (acid maltase)
cards.Extra: Image licensed by Physeo and used with permission. Purchase full access here.

cards.Text: Pompe disease is associated with {{c1::hypertrophic}} cardiomyopathy and hypotonia
cards.Extra: Pompe trashes the Pump (heart). Image licensed by Physeo and used with permission. Purchase full access here.

cards.Text: {{c2::Cori}} disease (glycogen storage disease type {{c1::III}}) is deficiency of {{c3::debranching enzyme}}
cards.Extra: Accumulates limit dextrin; normal lactate, milder than von Gierke. Image licensed by Physeo and used with permission. Purchase full access here.

cards.Text: {{c2::Andersen}} disease (glycogen storage disease type {{c1::IV}}) is deficiency of {{c3::branching enzyme}}
cards.Extra: ABCD: Andersen, Branching / Cori, Debranching. Cirrhosis in infancy. Image licensed by Physeo and used with permission. Purchase full access here.

cards.Text: {{c2::McArdle}} disease (glycogen storage disease type {{c1::V}}) is deficiency of muscle {{c3::glycogen phosphorylase}} (myophosphorylase)
cards.Extra: McArdle = Muscle. Image licensed by Physeo and used with permission. Purchase full access here.

cards.Text: McArdle disease presents with exercise intolerance and {{c1::no rise in lactate}} on exertion
cards.Extra: Cramps, myoglobinuria, second-wind phenomenon. Image licensed by Physeo and used with permission. Purchase full access here.

cards.Text: {{c2::Hers}} disease (glycogen storage disease type {{c1::VI}}) is deficiency of liver {{c3::glycogen phosphorylase}}
cards.Extra: Mild: hepatomegaly, mild hypoglycemia, normal lactate. Image licensed by Physeo and used with permission. Purchase full access here.

cards.Text: In the fed state, glycogen synthesis is driven by {{c1::insulin}}
cards.Extra: Image licensed by Physeo and used with permission. Purchase full access here.

cards.Text: In the fasting state, liver glycogenolysis is driven by {{c1::glucagon}}
cards.Extra: Image licensed by Physeo and used with permission. Purchase full access here.

cards.Text: Liver glycogen is largely depleted after about {{c1::12-24}} hours of fasting
cards.Extra: Gluconeogenesis then dominates. Image licensed by Physeo and used with permission. Purchase full access here.

cards.Text: The bond broken by glycogen phosphorylase is {{c1::α-1,4}}, not α-1,6
cards.Extra: α-1,6 is handled by the debranching enzyme. Image licensed by Physeo and used with permission. Purchase full access here.

cards.Text: Glucose-1-phosphate from glycogenolysis enters glycolysis after conversion to {{c1::glucose-6-phosphate}}
cards.Extra: By phosphoglucomutase. Image licensed by Physeo and used with permission. Purchase full access here.

cards.Text: The Ca2+ sensor subunit of phosphorylase kinase is {{c1::calmodulin}}
cards.Extra: Couples muscle contraction to glycogenolysis. Image licensed by Physeo and used with permission. Purchase full access here.

cards.Text: The two enzymatic activities of the debranching enzyme are 4-α-glucanotransferase and {{c1::α-1,6-glucosidase}}
cards.Extra: Image licensed by Physeo and used with permission. Purchase full access here.

cards.Text: Insulin, acting on liver, {{c1::in}}creases glycogenesis and {{c1::de}}creases glycogenolysis
cards.Extra: Image licensed by Physeo and used with permission. Purchase full access here.

cards.Text: Thyroid hormone increases {{c1::glycogenolysis}} and gluconeogenesis
cards.Extra: Catabolic effect. Image licensed by Physeo and used with permission. Purchase full access here.
